messages.author: 4a0898d2dc141e12
messages.subject: masking probes with aroma
parts:
What ist the best way in aroma.affymetrix to exclude certain probes?

What I need to do is:
- Load CEL Data
- Perform BG correction and Quantile normalization
- Look at the CEL Data and identify misbehaving probes
- Remove the misbehaving probes
- Perform again BG correction and Quantile normalization using only
the good probes
- Perform RMA summary.

Would be nice, if you could give me some hints?

best regards,
hubert

messages.author: a5f6afcbe5b17914
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] masking probes with aroma
parts:
Hi,

unlike units ("probe sets"), there is no method for masking out
certain *cells ("probes")* in the analysis. It's been requested and
discussed before, but we had no time to implement it.

However, one possible approach is to assign NA to cell intensities you
wish to exclude. This will work with method that detects and ignores
NA intensities. Many/most of the methods I have implemented do this,
but do not have a list of validated methods. I know for sure that the
RMA-style probe summary methods works.

In order to assign NAs, you basically have to do:

# SAFETY: Do not update CEL files in rawData/
stopifnot(basename(getParent(getPath(cs), 2)) != "rawData");

# Indices of cells to be assigned NA
cells <- c(1005,1032,514,45050);
signals <- rep(as.double(NA), length(cells));

# Write these signals to each CEL file
for (kk in seq(cs)) {
cf <- getFile(cs, kk);
updateCel(getPathname(cf), indices=cells, intensities=signals);
}

So be careful not to update your original CEL files in rawData/. I
recommend that after you located the "bad" probes, create a copy of
your data set in rawData/ to probeData/ (where all normalized data
sets end up anyway) and add a tag, e.g.

probaData/MyData,hasNAs/...

and work from that one.

Please let me know how it works.

/Henrik

messages.author: 4a0898d2dc141e12
messages.subject: Re: masking probes with aroma
parts:
Finally, I did it by using the restructor functionality of the CDF.
Works fine. Okay, you have to clear the caches after that, because
some objects are out of sync if you remove probes from the CDF.

regards,
hubert
